$comment: Documentation overlay for the PixStorage SQLite schema of PIX timing captures. Everything here was observed on PIX 2606.18-preview captures taken by this server; integer codes are recorded as observed and never decoded. Timestamps are capture-clock nanoseconds.
notes: Timestamps and durations are capture-clock nanoseconds; CaptureFacts 12 records 1000000000 ticks per second.

Row ids are not OS ids: ApiQueueExecution.ThreadId, PixCpuMarker.ThreadId, PixCpuExecution.ThreadRowId and ReadyThread.ReadyingThreadRowId are Threads.Id; ApiCommandQueue.ProcessId and PixCounterInfo.ProcessId are Processes.Id. StackEvents.OSThreadId and Images.OSProcessId are OS ids.
ProcThreadId columns pack the OS process id in the high 32 bits and the OS thread id in the low 32 bits (0 = idle).

Virtual tables (ContextSwitch, ReadyThread-backed ranges, PixCpuExecution, ...) decode BLOB ranges on the fly: constrain Timestamp/BeginTimestamp, Core or thread columns so PixStorage can push the filter down (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows VIRTUAL TABLE INDEX).
Nested PIX executions (Level > 0) overlap their parents: sum siblings, never ancestors.

facts.2: First reliable timestamp (ns): recorded data before it can be incomplete.
facts.3: Capture end timestamp (ns): the last recorded data; the default end of $end in rangeMode=full.
facts.4: Target process id (OS pid) of the capture.
facts.5: Logical core count (observed 32 on a 32-thread machine).
facts.24: Capture stop timestamp (ns): the end of the reliable window ($reliableEnd, rangeMode=reliable).

functions.findstackid/2: findstackid(osThreadId, timestamp) returns the Stacks.Id recorded for that OS thread at exactly that timestamp (StackEvents), or 0/NULL when none; use the OS thread id (ProcThreadId & 4294967295) and a CpuSample or ContextSwitch timestamp.

CaptureFacts.purpose: Numeric capture facts by id; see facts for documented ids.

CaptureData.purpose: Capture metadata as string pairs: stop time, target process id and name, PIX version, OS, CPU, memory, machine, GPU info, capture options.
joins: JOIN Strings n ON n.Id = CaptureData.NameId JOIN Strings v ON v.Id = CaptureData.ValueId

CaptureStats.purpose: Recording statistics per interval: ETW events and bytes written, lost ETW events and buffers.
caveats: Non-zero lost counts mean every count and duration derived from ETW is a lower bound.

DroppedData.purpose: Ranges where the recorder dropped data, per lane and type (8603 rows observed, types 3 and 7).

columns.LaneId: Lane the drop applies to (as recorded).
columns.Type: Drop type code as recorded (not decoded).

TruncatedData.purpose: Counts of data the recorder truncated, per id as recorded.

Strings.purpose: Interned strings; most *NameId, *TypeId and *PathId columns reference Strings.Id.

SymbolStrings.purpose: Interned symbol strings (function and source names); FunctionInformation.DecoratedNameId references SymbolStrings.Id.

Processes.purpose: Processes seen during the capture. Id is the row id other tables reference; ProcessId is the OS pid.

Threads.purpose: Threads seen during the capture with lifetime and per-thread counts. Id is the thread row id used by execution, marker, submission and ready-thread tables.

columns.ThreadNameId: Strings.Id of the thread name (empty string when unnamed).
columns.PixEventCount: PIX CPU events recorded on the thread.

joins: JOIN Processes p ON p.Id = Threads.ProcessRowId
LEFT JOIN Strings s ON s.Id = Threads.ThreadNameId

Cores.purpose: Logical cores with per-core context switch and sample counts.
joins: JOIN PhysicalCores pc ON pc.Id = Cores.PhysicalCoreId

PhysicalCores.purpose: Physical cores with their efficiency class (heterogeneous P/E cores differ; all 0 on homogeneous CPUs).

columns.EfficiencyClass: Efficiency class as reported by Windows (higher = more performant).

ApiCommandQueue.purpose: D3D command queues of recorded processes: type and name, lifetime, execution and command list counts.

columns.TypeId: Strings.Id of the queue type (Direct, Compute, Copy).
columns.ProcessId: Processes.Id (row id, not the OS pid).

joins: JOIN Processes p ON p.Id = ApiCommandQueue.ProcessId
LEFT JOIN Strings s ON s.Id = ApiCommandQueue.NameId

ApiQueueExecution.purpose: One row per ExecuteCommandLists: submit timestamp on the CPU and the GPU begin/end of the work it carried. The real GPU timeline of a timing capture.

columns.ThreadId: Threads.Id of the submitting thread (row id).
columns.FrameToken: Frame token as recorded (0 when unset).

joins: JOIN ApiCommandQueue q ON q.Id = ApiQueueExecution.ApiCommandQueueId
JOIN Threads t ON t.Id = ApiQueueExecution.ThreadId
JOIN ApiQueueExecutionCommandList l ON l.ApiQueueExecutionId = ApiQueueExecution.Id
caveats: Executions on one queue can overlap; compute busy time as the union of intervals (see the gpu_busy_per_queue named query).

ApiQueueExecutionCommandList.purpose: Command lists of each ApiQueueExecution: count and a BLOB of command list ids.

columns.CommandLists: BLOB of command list identifiers (not decoded).

GpuWorkRange.purpose: Hardware queue work as long range containers: each row spans many packets and stores them in the Work BLOB (15 rows observed for a 4-second capture).
caveats: Rows are containers, not individual GPU work items; do not treat EndTimestamp - BeginTimestamp as busy time.

HardwareCommandQueue.purpose: Hardware (kernel) queues per adapter: 3D, COPY, Compute, Video, 3DNodeXX.

HardwareAdapter.purpose: GPU adapters present during the capture.

GpuFrame.purpose: Present/flip timing per frame (DXGI frame statistics).
caveats: API-taken timing captures leave GpuFrame empty or all NULL; use VSync CustomMarker rows or ApiQueueExecution cadence for frames.

CustomMarker.purpose: Custom marker timestamps, including VSync per monitor (CustomMarkerInfo name 'VSync').
joins: JOIN CustomMarkerInfo i ON i.Id = CustomMarker.MarkerInfoId JOIN Strings s ON s.Id = i.NameId
Interval per monitor: Timestamp - LAG(Timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY MarkerInfoId ORDER BY Timestamp)

CustomMarkerInfo.purpose: Custom marker kinds: name (VSync) and the data type (monitor) they belong to.

CustomDataTypeInfo.purpose: Custom data lanes such as 'Monitor #{}1' with the GPU driving it in SubNameId.

PixEventInfo.purpose: Distinct PIX event names with CPU and GPU occurrence counts.

PixMarkerInfo.purpose: Distinct PIX marker (PIXSetMarker) names with CPU and GPU counts.

PixExecutionRange.purpose: BLOB containers backing the PixCpuExecution virtual table, per thread row and nesting level.

PixCpuMarkerRange.purpose: BLOB containers backing the PixCpuMarker virtual table, per thread row.

PixGpuMarker.purpose: GPU-side PIX markers per API command queue; empty unless the application emits GPU PIX markers.

GpuExecutionRange.purpose: BLOB containers backing PixGpuExecution; empty unless the application emits GPU PIX events.

CpuGpuExecutionMap.purpose: Maps CPU PIX markers to GPU events; empty without GPU-side PIX markers.
caveats: CPU-to-GPU causality is only available when this table has rows.

ApiMarkerGpuWorkMap.purpose: Maps API markers to GPU work; empty without GPU-side markers.

PixCounterGroup.purpose: Counter groups: custom counters and 'GPU Memory (Adapter #N)' groups.

columns.ParentGroupId: PixCounterGroup.Id of the parent (NULL at the root).

PixCounterInfo.purpose: Recorded counters: custom PIXReportCounter counters and GPU memory Local/Non-Local Budget, Usage and Resident per adapter.

columns.UnitsId: Strings.Id of the unit (MB for GPU memory, empty for custom counters).

joins: JOIN PixCounters c ON c.CounterId = PixCounterInfo.Id

PixCounterRange.purpose: BLOB containers backing the PixCounters virtual table.

CpuSample.purpose: CPU samples: core, timestamp and the sampled thread (ProcThreadId 0 = idle).

Stacks.purpose: Unique call stacks: frame count and a BLOB of 64-bit return addresses (leaf first).

StackEvents.purpose: Per OS thread ranges mapping stack-capturing events to Stacks; read through findstackid.

columns.OSThreadId: OS thread id (not a Threads row id).

Images.purpose: Loaded images per OS process with load address, size and lifetime.

Modules.purpose: PE modules with PDB identity (path, GUID, age).

FunctionInformation.purpose: Resolved functions per module: offset, size and decorated name; empty until symbols are resolved.

SourceFile.purpose: Source files referenced by resolved line information.

SourceLine.purpose: Source line ranges per module offset for resolved symbols.

ReadyThread.purpose: Ready-thread events: when a thread was made runnable, on which core, and by which thread (385243 rows observed).

columns.ReadyingThreadRowId: Threads.Id of the thread that readied it.

joins: ContextSwitch.ReadyThreadId = ReadyThread.Id links a switch-in to the ready event that preceded it.

ContextSwitchRange.purpose: BLOB containers per core backing the ContextSwitch virtual table.

ContextSwitchRangeThread.purpose: Per range and thread switch counts, an index over ContextSwitchRange.

FileIORange.purpose: File I/O containers per device backing the FileEvents virtual table; empty unless file I/O was captured.

Win32Device.purpose: Devices seen by file I/O capture.

FileInfo.purpose: Files seen by file I/O capture.

MemoryEventRanges.purpose: Memory event containers backing the CpuMemoryEvent virtual table; empty unless memory events were captured.

MemoryPairing.purpose: Commit/decommit pairs for memory events; empty unless memory events were captured.

Budgets.purpose: Budget descriptors by type and source as recorded.

ContextSwitch.purpose: Context switches decoded from ContextSwitchRange: core, timestamp, the thread switched out and in, priorities, the wait reason of the thread switched out and the ready event (634626 rows observed).

columns.FromProcThreadId: OS pid << 32 | OS tid switched out (0 = idle).
columns.ToProcThreadId: OS pid << 32 | OS tid switched in.
columns.ReadyThreadId: ReadyThread.Id of the ready event for the incoming thread (0 when none).
columns.FromThreadWaitReason: KWAIT_REASON code of the outgoing thread as recorded (not decoded).

caveats: Always constrain Timestamp (and Core or ToProcThreadId when possible); PixStorage pushes those down.

PixCpuExecution.purpose: PIX CPU events (PIXBeginEvent/PIXEndEvent) with nesting level, thread row and color.
joins: JOIN PixEventInfo i ON i.Id = PixCpuExecution.EventId JOIN Strings s ON s.Id = i.NameId
JOIN Threads t ON t.Id = PixCpuExecution.ThreadRowId
caveats: rowid values are range-encoded (observed from 5000), not 1..n.

PixCpuExecutionTimes.purpose: Execution and stall split of each PIX CPU event: Duration = Execution + Stall.

Execution.description: Time the thread was running inside the event.

Stall.description: Time the thread was not running inside the event.

columns.CpuExecutionRowId: Hidden constraint column naming a PixCpuExecution rowid; NULL/0 unless constrained.

caveats: Constrain CpuExecutionRowId with = and one value per lookup: a correlated scalar subquery (SELECT Execution FROM PixCpuExecutionTimes t WHERE t.CpuExecutionRowId = e.rowid) matched all 868 events on 2606.18, but joins, IN lists, json_each and VALUES lists on it returned a single row.
Matching on (EventId, BeginTimestamp, EndTimestamp) is fast when tuples are unique; check Execution + Stall = Duration either way.

PixCpuMarker.purpose: PIX CPU point markers (PIXSetMarker) with timestamp and thread row.

PixGpuExecution.purpose: GPU-side PIX events per API command queue.
caveats: Empty unless the application emits GPU PIX events; GPU work is in ApiQueueExecution.

PixCounters.purpose: Counter samples (step values) decoded from PixCounterRange.

columns.Value: Sample value in the counter's unit.

caveats: A value holds until the next sample of the same counter.

FileEvents.purpose: File I/O operations with device, file, thread, offset, size and status; empty unless file I/O was captured.

CpuMemoryEvent.purpose: CPU memory allocation and free events; empty unless memory events were captured.
